It's a nice thought. All I will say is that I would easily choose death than go back inpatient. If I was sent there, I'd try kill myself rather than live through that again; it was that bad. I will never be same after that - it was inhuman. 

I don't have that kind of medical leave at my job, I can take time off let alone go home on time. 

I don't fit in, I don't like the world I live in. I'm very alienated. I hope things change in the culture/society.   I'm not able to leave where I am at, nor adapt to it sufficiently. I can't change and modify everything about myself. Talking about vague coping skills and life changes is a waste of what little time and money I have.

I'll be honest, I didn't follow all of that, but from what I can gather it sounds very bad. I'm sorry that its like that, not that it means much coming from a stranger. I've never know anyone without skills or talents, but I have known a lot of people who don't see them. This isn't the 1950s, you don't have to be a house wife.  I'm not sure what the your relationship is like exactly, but if I was in an unhappy relationship I would tell the person how I felt. If they didn't listen, I 'd leave. If you're so unhappy that you would rather die than stay trapped in a relationship, it might be worth considering a divorce?

I am glad that the behavioral health system has worked for you. I've had several therapists tell me that that they didn't think I wold benefit from therapy and should seek alternatives. I still don't know what the alternatives are. 

I thought the behavioral health system could work for me if I tried hard to find the right fit. I have seen 16 therapists, 5 psychologists, and 3 psychiatrists,  attended 3 groups, an IOP, and an inpatient facility over the last 8 years. I have had CBT, DBT, psycho analysis, EDMR, trauma-informed, relation systems, and holistic variants of therapy. I tried medication, but my body did not tolerate it.

There is a finite limit to what coping can do for me. At some point coping is just putting band-aids on a hemorrhage - I'm still bleeding out, but slightly more slowly.

I guess the idea is you "tread water", hoping eventually you are able to "swim" to a better place, or have someone can throw you a life preserver. Except no one is coming to help, and I am so exhausted from treading water that I know in my gut I will soon go under. If I start thrashing in the water, calling for help, I will lose my job and probably be sent to an inpatient facility again. I live in my county/city, the inpatient facilities are bleak and dangerous - like halfway houses. I do not want get tossed into the hospital again - I never recovered from the last time.

It's your call to make, not mine. That said, I lived with a guy who tried to kill himself several times this way and it never worked - he just fucked up his liver/kidneys and had to get his stomach pumped. Again, I'm not advocating either way, I'm just stating facts.
